_meta.note: Reference bands for the narrator and the game's financial code. Real figures vary widely; these are realistic typical ranges.

indonesia.naturalised heritage players: Already at European clubs; no fee involved for national team purposes

asia.J1/K1 → Europe (good player): €1M-15M (Japanese players often move cheaply to Belgium/Scotland/Netherlands first)
asia.Chinese Super League: Mostly frees and low fees since the salary cap

europe.Championship / 2nd tiers: €500K-10M (Championship pays far more than other 2nd tiers)
europe.Recent largest: Alexander Isak to Liverpool 2025 (~£125M), Florian Wirtz to Liverpool 2025 (~£100M+)

indonesia_IDR_per_month.Liga 4 (amateur): Rp 0-2M (often only match fees and transport)

currencyApprox.note: Approximate exchange rates for display only (late 2025). The game should store wealth in one base currency and convert.

incomeTax.Spain: ~47% top (Beckham Law special regime abolished for footballers in 2015)
incomeTax.Italy: ~43% top (Decreto Crescita foreign-player tax break abolished in 2024)
incomeTax.USA: Federal up to 37% + state (Florida/Texas 0% state tax)

agents.typicalCut: 5-10% of wage (FIFA agent regulations cap fees at 3-5% of remuneration for most deals since 2023, though enforcement is contested)
agents.storyNote: Bad or fake agents exploiting young players from Southeast Asia, Africa and South America are a real problem — a strong source of drama for fictional agents.
